This is for a long thread of stories of the 600 lb man across from my hospital bed.

After my long fight with the hamgalaxy across from me, finally one of us is moving! And it's not the ham. Of course. There are no cranes available to move him just yet.

It's been a wonderful journey, so I will leave you with a short story and just random shit the fat has said.

Things the fat has said that made me choke on air:

-" If I get my weight loss surgery and lose about 100 lbs, I could easily be a top fighter. Probably a boxer or MMA." *He's about 650 lbs.

-"Being a truck driver was a physically hard job. A lot of weight I gained was muscle before I got fired."

-"I don't even like sugary foods, which are supposed to be bad for you. I eat protein most of the time. Protien builds muscles. So my muscles are all fit."

-"Doctors just lie about things. They say everything is because I'm overweight. Everyone gets pneumonia. Thin people have diabetes. I know a healthy guy who works out every day who has AFib too. I'd still have these things if I wasn't big"

-"I can't drink tea. It's disgusting. It's just like drinking sewer water. Mom, go to the vending machine and grab me a coke."

-"I wasn't able to finish the vegetables. There was nothing on them! No one gave me any sauce to put on them."

-"I feel faint, my blood sugar is getting low. I need my sandwich now! yells at nurse"

-"REE3EEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEE"

Now here's the last little story.

Two days ago was my 22 birthday. My family and friends are pretty far away, so I didn't have any visitors or cards or anything. But one nurse, who I've gotten to be pretty good with, brought me some vegan snacks her boyfriend made because they're vegans. It was really good. I could see fatty fat fat over there eyeing my treats. I knew I was safe because the chances of him becoming mobile are as likely as the chances of dinosaurs becoming reincarnated and dancing the Can Can. (Actually the dinosaur thing might have more of a chance.)

So I made sure to enjoy my treat out in the open. I only had two of the little squares and then I safely put it back in my drawer to bug the fatty with day after day.

But he did get pissed, and started to try and tourment back. He asked me how old I was. I said I was 22. Then periodically throughout the day he would ask little things like "Is your family coming to visit?" "Any friends coming by today?" "Have you got any cards yet?" Sometimes I would answer, sometimes I would ignore him. By the end of the day though, he asked his mom to grab his pile of birthday cards he got a while back. He started going through them, reading loudly the things they said inside. He counted them. He talked about how lucky he was to have so many friends. I didn't have any cards, and I knew he was doing it on purpose. You know, like 2 year olds do.

He kept talking about how many cards he had, blah blah blah. Finally I just said "maybe you got so many cards because people think this will be your last birthday."

He just smiles and goes "It's okay to be jealous."

I said "I'm not jealous of someone who has to call a nurse every time he shits himself or someone who has to have validation of his existence through other people sending him cardboard with birthday picture on it. One day I'm going to go home, be active, be healthy again, and have a meaningful and productive life. You will never have that."

He yells across the room, scaring everyone "I was productive before you were even born! I've done more things than you can ever hope! I used to drive transport deliveries into military bases delivering dangerous weapons! I served our country and helped fight against terrorists." (He literally means by driving a transport truck)

So I yelled back (well I wheezed back. I can't really yell) "And now look at you! Fat, entitled, lazy pig who takes advantage of doctors and nurses who only try to help you! You are a waste of resources and most of your problems could be solved by losing weight!"

He starts to shout back something about growing up and being a hard worker and how I'm in the "same position" he's in, but a few nurses ran in and closed the curtains, talking to us individually to get us to calm down. I could still here the galaxy shouting once in a while.

So my curtain stays closed, and I'm transferring to a new hospital in a couple days to see about a lung transplant.

I wanted to go out with a bang. And even though the fight left me shaking hard and not able to breathe, I got time out of the room, and I feel like it was a small victory against entitled fats everywhere.

I love you, shitlords and shitladies.
